business_problem: Delphi needed an autonomous driving system that could operate safely in real-world conditions where no fixed rule set exists for every scenario, while still being suitable for large-scale vehicle deployment.
solution_summary: Delphi built its Centralized Sensing Localization Planning platform (CSLP) as a hybrid autonomous-driving stack that combines predefined safety rules with AI-based decisioning. The implementation ingests signals from three sensor types—radar, vision cameras, and LiDAR—to create a redundant perception layer with complementary strengths: radar for weather tolerance, LiDAR for precise range and distance, and vision for object classification. Sensor inputs are fused inside the platform to increase confidence in the vehicle’s understanding of its surroundings. AI is used primarily in the vision pipeline, where machine-learning models and an onboard neural net are trained to recognize objects and classify them in real time. The platform then applies generalized rules plus AI-driven path selection to choose safe actions, while fleet-collected driving data is used to catalog new scenarios and improve how the system reacts when conditions are not already covered by rules.

data_flow: Radar, vision-camera, and LiDAR data are collected on the vehicle and fused by Delphi's CSLP platform to build a high-confidence view of the surroundings. The vision stream feeds AI and machine-learning models, including an onboard neural net for real-time object classification. The platform combines those outputs with generalized driving rules to choose a path, while fleet data is used to expand scenario coverage and improve future responses.
business_outcome: Delphi reports that the hybrid AI-and-rules approach gives the vehicle a more comprehensive view of its surroundings, improves object recognition and path decisions, and adds redundant safety with a safe-stop response when scenarios are not recognized.
